what: How each Alabama place voted in five contests of the 2020, 2022 and 2024 general elections: the votes for the Democratic ticket, the Republican ticket, every other candidate and all write-ins together, and the total, added up from the Alabama Secretary of State's official precinct results, county by county.
note: What this is: how the people of a place voted in that election, in the Secretary of State's official precinct results with each county's absentee and provisional ballots, added up here by county, by judicial circuit (whole counties) and, for 2022 and 2024, for the two state Senate districts made of whole counties; each statewide sum equals the State Canvassing Board's certified canvass. Alabama reports absentee and provisional ballots for each county as a whole and many precincts lie in two districts, so a district that is not made of whole counties cannot be added up without estimating, and none is given. What this is not: it is not a prediction of any election; it says nothing about any candidate on a later ballot or about any voter; a nonpartisan office stays nonpartisan; and a district's figures are for the lines of that year. The tickets are named only to say which election this was. In a place with very few voters the split would come close to saying how particular people voted, so there the split is left out.

few.why: A place's too_few lists the contests in which it had fewer than 20 votes, or in which every vote went the same way. There the split comes close to saying how particular people voted, so a page should leave it out. The counts are the official record all the same, and are kept here so that the sums can be checked.

not_given: Cities and towns: Alabama's cities and towns elect their officers at municipal elections apart from November, our places hold none, and a precinct may lie partly inside a city. School districts: the results do not name them, and a county board of education's district is not the county where a city runs its own schools. County commission districts, state House districts and the state Senate districts not made of whole counties: Alabama reports absentee and provisional ballots for each county as a whole, and in 2022 260 precincts carried the contests of two or more House districts, 108 of two or more Senate districts and 269 of two commission districts (the results give such a precinct's votes whole), so these cannot be added up without estimating. State Board of Education districts: they divide counties too. Districts in 2020: other lines.

senate.what: State Senate districts of the plan first used in 2022, where made of whole counties
senate.why_not: Senate districts are given for 2022 and 2024 only: the 2020 election was held on the districts drawn in 2011.
senate.note: A state Senate district is given only where it is made of whole counties: every precinct of each of its counties voted in that district's contest in 2022 and in no other Senate district's. That holds for 2 of the 35 (District 4 (Cullman, Marion and Winston counties) and District 23 (Butler, Clarke, Conecuh, Dallas, Lowndes, Monroe, Perry and Wilcox counties)); the others are not given, because Alabama reports absentee and provisional ballots for each county as a whole and 108 precincts carried the contests of two or more Senate districts in 2022 (the results give such a precinct's votes whole), so their votes cannot be added up without estimating.

house.what: State House districts of the plan first used in 2022
house.why_not: No state House district is given: none is made of whole counties, Alabama reports absentee and provisional ballots for each county as a whole, and 260 precincts carried the contests of two or more House districts in 2022 (the results give such a precinct's votes whole), so a House district's votes cannot be added up without estimating.
house.note: No state House district is given: none is made of whole counties, Alabama reports absentee and provisional ballots for each county as a whole, and 260 precincts carried the contests of two or more House districts in 2022 (the results give such a precinct's votes whole), so a House district's votes cannot be added up without estimating.

com.why_not: County commission districts are not given: Alabama reports absentee and provisional ballots for each county as a whole, so no district inside a county can be added up whole from the precinct results (and in 2022 269 precincts carried the contests of two commission districts).
